findings.finding: J2 and J3 have a circular ordering dependency: J2 must move `_sanitize_description` / `_sanitize_comment` into `jira_family/` parameterized by the `RichTextCodec` Protocol, but J3 defines that Protocol inside `adapters/jira_family/` — the very package J2 creates. J3 lists J2 ([rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743]) as a dependency for the package's existence, while J2's body references J3 ([rebar:aac8-b283-22c1-4e66]) for the Protocol's definition. J2's only mitigation is a `Callable[[str], str]` stopgap, which creates a two-phase rework cycle (J2 lands with a stub, then J2 is re-opened when J3 lands to widen to the full Protocol) — an unacknowledged rework burden not reflected in either story's AC or scope.

findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) move the `RichTextCodec` Protocol definition into J2's scope (J2 creates the package and the Protocol skeleton; J3 adds AdfCodec and WikiTextCodec implementations on top of it), or (b) declare J3 a strict prerequisite of J2 and remove the Callable fallback language from J2. findings.finding: The plan declares that the DC backend 'requires https' but does not declare the TLS certificate verification posture. Self-hosted Jira DC instances commonly use self-signed or internal-CA certificates. If the pycontribs/jira client silently disables certificate verification (verify=False) to accommodate these, or if the plan intends to add a bypass flag without documenting it, MITM attacks on the corporate network path become feasible. The plan is silent on whether cert validation is enforced, whether a custom CA bundle path is configurable, and whether a 'skip_verify' escape hatch is planned — leaving the actual TLS security guarantee undeclared.
findings.location: Approach §7 (Security posture for the DC connection); AC item: 'The DC backend rejects a non-https reconciler.base_url unless allow_insecure = true is set'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to §7: 'TLS certificate verification is enforced by default (pycontribs/jira verify=True). Operators with self-signed or internal-CA certificates supply a CA bundle path via reconciler.ca_bundle; rebar passes it as verify=<path> to the jira client. A reconciler.skip_tls_verify = true escape hatch is supported for non-production use and emits a WARNING identical in severity to allow_insecure.' Add a corresponding AC bullet. This keeps the private-network threat model sound without blocking legitimate self-signed-cert deployments.

findings.finding: The Approach explicitly defers folding `config.py`'s third copy of the local→Jira status map into the single `jira_family` definition to bug `fe15`, yet the 'Exactly one dict literal' AC asserts 'across the whole engine' with no carve-out for `config.py`. An implementer who satisfies the Approach (leaves `config.py` alone) will fail the AC; one who satisfies the AC will exceed the stated scope.
findings.location: Approach §2 ('This epic consolidates the two `adapters/` copies; `config.py`'s is folded in by bug `fe15`') vs. AC 'Exactly one dict literal defines the local→Jira status map and one the priority map across the whole engine'

findings.finding: The plan correctly identifies that DC resolved-status names are site-variable ('a self-hosted DC workflow can name its resolved states anything') and parameterizes `classify_probe_response` to accept the set as input, but never specifies WHERE or HOW an operator configures their DC resolved-status set. If the DC adapter hardcodes a default frozenset with no config-schema knob, operators with custom workflows cannot fix misclassification without code changes.
findings.location: Approach §2 — `classify_probe_response` parameterization; AC line 'No mapping logic exists in two places'
findings.suggested_fix: Add `resolved_status_names: list[str] = ["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"]` to the `jira-datacenter` config block in `_config_schema.py`, pass it as the frozenset argument to `classify_probe_response` in the DC backend constructor, and add an AC line: 'DC backend passes `reconciler.resolved_status_names` (defaulting to ["Resolved","Done","Cancelled"]) to `classify_probe_response`; operator docs list the knob and its default.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how `outbound_fields.py`'s new `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import ...` import is made safe in the standalone-load (spec_from_file_location without package context) path — either by adding the same bootstrap try/except pattern already present for `_loader`, or by confirming that the J2 story must also update all standalone-load call sites to inject `jira_family` into sys.modules first.
evidence: Plan: 'Editing a pinned module's *contents* (e.g. replacing a dict literal with an import) is safe'
outbound_fields.py:37-49 shows the module has a try/except bootstrap for `_loader` when loaded without package context via spec_from_file_location
ADR 0035 §(a): 'outbound_fields.py' is in the location-pinned set loaded by spec_from_file_location
The plan does not mention adding a similar bootstrap for the new `jira_family` import inside the pinned module
findings.finding: When `outbound_fields.py` (location-pinned, loaded by `spec_from_file_location` without package context in tests) gains a new `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import ...` import to single-source the value maps, that import will fail in the standalone-load path unless the same bootstrap pattern already used for `rebar_reconciler._loader` is added. The plan says 'editing a pinned module's contents is safe' but does not address this standalone-load edge case — tests that load `outbound_fields.py` via `spec_from_file_location` would fail with ImportError on the new `jira_family` import even though the file path hasn't moved.
findings.location: Approach §2, 'Stays put (path-wise)' and 'Move by SYMBOL, not by file' subsections; outbound_fields.py bootstrap pattern at lines 37-49
scenarios: Any test that loads outbound_fields.py via spec_from_file_location or the lazy_load path (i.e. without full rebar_reconciler package context) would hit ImportError on `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira_family import _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` when jira_family is not in sys.modules

The existing test_config.py:193 (`_load_attr('adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py', '_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS')`) would fail if the attribute is now an imported name and the file-path load lacks the jira_family package
findings.suggested_fix: In the J2 story, require that the new import of jira_family symbols in outbound_fields.py be wrapped in the same try/except bootstrap pattern already used for `rebar_reconciler._loader` (lines 37-49 of outbound_fields.py), loading jira_family's __init__ by file path as a fallback when the normal import fails — mirroring the existing pattern exactly.
